body: Looking at the referenced [cpp code](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8b2739ee55f8bebe7c4a20c55841851c4f411efe/scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp#L1163) (which I am far from good at reading), it looks like it is not traversing ancestors to find a nested or root state machine before trying to make a playback path.  If that's correct then it seems like the source of my issue and that the documentation referencing ancestors (blend tree or otherwise) isn't accurate?
Please upload an MRP to help investigating this, it's far more efficient for our maintainers to have something to test directly

> Please upload an MRP to help investigating this, it's far more efficient for our maintainers to have something to test directly

I think I more or less answered my own question:

Documentation says (emphasis mine):
> There must be a state machine with state_machine_type of STATE_MACHINE_TYPE_ROOT or STATE_MACHINE_TYPE_NESTED in the parent **or ancestor**.

[Code says:](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8b2739ee55f8bebe7c4a20c55841851c4f411efe/scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp#L1163)
- Remove the last split before "/playback"
- add "/playback" back on
- get the playback if it isn't null -- it isn't checking multiple ancestors.

In my case, I have a blend tree between the two state machines, so there is not a a playback on this call `Ref<AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback> playback = p_tree->get(playback_path);`

There would be if the string manipulation was performed again going up the path one more level and re-appending "/playback" and playback was checked again, though.

It *seems* like the solution to make it match the docs and provide more functionality is to make it recursively look up the path for a playback, but there may be other things that need to change elsewhere.

Either way, I can try to make an MRP when I have time.

[descedendant_grouped_animation_tree_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21532454/descedendant_grouped_animation_tree_mrp.zip) A bit more than an MRP, because I wanted to demonstrate working variations of the same state machine, just with a direct descendant or a type other than grouped. **TLDR: press shift+z, shift+x, or shift+y and the error will be output:** ----- Overview: - This project has an AnimationTree with a top level AnimationNodeBlendTree. - That blend tree has a single state machine (root_state). - The root_state state machine has three child state machines, demonstrating different ways to configure a child/descendant state machine. - `scale_descendant_grouped_state` is the one that is broken and cannot get a playback - The outer `root_state` machine translates the sphere along an axis - The inner state machines scale the sphere along an axis - Transitions into and out of the inner state machines is restricted to the end of animations (that is, the scale is 1,1,1 or the sphere is at the origin). The desired outcome here is to be able to with a single `travel` call, travel into and out of the inner state machine without teleporting, and be able to blend with the inner state machines independently (e.g. a descendant rather than a direct child). Inputs: - `root_state` machine. - The Z, X, and Y (or C) keys will travel `root_state` and translate the sphere along the respective axis. - Inner state machine (scale the sphere along the selected axis): - `scale_descendant_grouped_state`: This state is a blend tree that contains a **descendant** machine of type `Grouped` - Shift+Z, Shift+X, Shift+Y transition into and change states in this machine - **This is broken and logs errors** - `scale_child_grouped_state`: This state is a blend tree that contains a **child** machine of type `Grouped` - Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+X, and Ctrl+Y transition into and change states in this machine - This works as expected, but you cannot blend with the inner state machine independently of the outer - `scale_descendant_nested_state`: This state is a blend tree that contains **descendant** machine of type `Nested` - Alt+Z, Alt+X, and Alt+Y transition into and change states in this machine - This works as expected but requires individual travel calls to each state machine to transition into and out of it - The two descendant state machines add a color blend, to demonstrate why we would want to do it this way (also, the color blend makes it obvious the the outer state machine has transitioned to `scale_descendant_grouped_state` despite not entering any state in that machine The reason it is desirable to have a descendant grouped state machine is twofold: - You can not add nodes to blend/add with the entirety of a direct child state machine, and would instead need to add and manage all those parameters for each state - The above is achievable with nested descendant state machines, but then you can not travel in and out of those machines with a single travel call, and must instead `travel` inner state machines to `End` and make a second `travel` call in outer state machines ---- Edit: Went ahead and created an trimmed it down to an actual MRP without all the comparative working examples and just the broken inner machine in case that was all too much above (shift+x,y,z to generate the error): [mrp without working comparisons](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21532513/descedendant_grouped_animation_tree_mrp2.zip)
